correctness.rationale: For every vector, m^n<=product<=m and max(m-m^n)=h_n at m=n^{-1/(n-1)}. Shifted min attains h_n/2 for real shifts, with rational approximation to that constant. On the singleton unit-loop model all non-expansive terms are 1-Lipschitz, so comparing the all-ones vector to the critical diagonal forces half the gap and the equality profile. Rational formulas give rational output on rational atomic inputs, whereas h_n/2 is irrational for n>=3 by rational-root theorem. On the singleton diagonal, plain Zadeh formulas are only 0,1-s,s,1 in the upper half, forcing error >=h_n. All quantifiers, endpoints and n=2 boundary are addressed in RESULT.md. The checker corroborates but is not the proof.

value.rationale: Product t-norm is a canonical alternative to Łukasiewicz strong conjunction, and the exact expressiveness cost of lacking product in Zadeh and non-expansive modal languages is a natural motivated question. The result solves all integer arities and exhibits a qualitative rational-versus-real definability phase transition at arity 3, with modal-depth immunity and exact diagonal rigidity. This is a structurally motivated comparison, not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
